explanation: Loki, usually male, turned himself into a mare to lure away the stallion of a giant building the walls of Asgard. The foal he later bore was Sleipnir.

claims.text: In Norse myth, Loki is the mother of Sleipnir, Odin's eight-legged horse.
Frigg, Freyja and Hel are not the mother of Sleipnir.
In the Prose Edda, Loki takes the form of a mare to lure away Svaðilfari, the stallion of the giant who is building the wall of Asgard.
Loki later gives birth to the foal Sleipnir.
